Use it for\\\\n  alarms on AWS/EBS metrics (VolumeReadOps, VolumeWriteOps, VolumeReadBytes,\\\\n  VolumeWriteBytes, VolumeQueueLength, VolumeTotalReadTime/WriteTime,\\\\n  VolumeAvgReadLatency, BurstBalance) or EBSIOBalance%/EBSByteBalance%; for sizing\\\\n  IOPS or throughput changes; for a volume modification that looks stuck or failed;\\\\n  for deciding which snapshots or AMIs are safe to delete or how to recover them;\\\\n  for KMS errors on encrypted volumes; for EBS quota or limit errors; for a jump in\\\\n  the EBS bill; and for a pre-launch EBS review. Do not use it for S3, EFS, FSx,\\\\n  instance store, or EC2 problems unrelated to EBS.\\\\nmetadata:\\\\n  author: dewavic\\\\n  version: \\\\\"1.0.0\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: \\\\\"CHAT, INCIDENT_RCA\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: \\\\\"Amazon EBS, Amazon EC2, Amazon CloudWatch, AWS KMS, AWS CloudTrail, Service Quotas\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: \\\\\"Storage\\\\\"\\\\n---\\\\n# Amazon EBS Expertise\\\\n\\\\nUse this skill to troubleshoot Amazon EBS problems and to review an account\\'s Amazon EBS setup. It has two modes. Troubleshoot mode answers \\\\\"something is wrong, why?\\\\\" through one of five paths and returns a fixed verdict. Review mode answers \\\\\"is my EBS setup healthy before something goes wrong?\\\\\" and returns a rated report. Both modes are read-only and share the same volume-type rules, instance limits and service rules. Load only the reference files the request needs.\\\\n\\\\n## When to Use This Skill\\\\n\\\\n- Storage-related slowness, timeouts or high I/O latency on an Amazon EC2 instance.\\\\n- An alarm on AWS/EBS metrics or on instance `EBSIOBalance%` / `EBSByteBalance%`.\\\\n- A volume modification that looks stuck, failed, or did not improve performance.\\\\n- Snapshot, AMI, Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager, AWS Backup or Recycle Bin questions, including which snapshots are safe to delete.\\\\n- Encrypted-volume access errors and AWS KMS questions for Amazon EBS.\\\\n- Amazon EBS cost increases, idle or over-provisioned volumes.\\\\n- An operation that failed on an Amazon EBS quota, or \\\\\"how close am I to my limits?\\\\\"\\\\n- A request to review Amazon EBS posture before a launch, migration or peak event.\\\\n\\\\nDo not use this skill for Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, Amazon FSx, instance store, or Amazon EC2 issues unrelated to Amazon EBS.\\\\n\\\\n## Prerequisites\\\\n\\\\n- Read-only permissions for the APIs listed in [references/data-collection.md](references/data-collection.md).\\\\n- AWS CloudTrail access is optional. The skill works without it.\\\\n- Mutating changes run only through directed actions (Agent Actions in the Operator Web App), which need their own role and operator approval on the approval card.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Workflow\\\\n\\\\nCopy this checklist and tick each step as you finish it:\\\\n\\\\n- [ ] Step 1: Classify the request\\\\n- [ ] Step 2: Load the shared references\\\\n- [references/review-operational.md](references/review-operational.md) and [references/review-report-format.md](references/review-report-format.md) |\\\\n\\\\nIf a request fits more than one row, answer Fix anything that fails, then present it.\\\\n\\\\n- Every number under Evidence came from an API call made in this session, has its unit and time window, and matches the resource ID it is attributed to.\\\\n- The Binding layer agrees with the Evidence: the named layer is the one at its limit, and the other layers were checked and shown to have headroom.\\\\n- Any Recommendation stays within the instance\\'s EBS baseline and the volume type\\'s documented limits, and it is not more provisioning for an impairment.\\\\n- Every \\\\\"safe to delete\\\\\" verdict is backed by the checks its tier requires; if one of those checks failed, the item is not safe to delete.\\\\n- A review answer starts with the Summary table and rates all six areas.\\\\n- Every API that failed or was not called is listed under Gaps.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Critical Rules\\\\n\\\\n- **Read-only.** Changes (ModifyVolume, DeleteSnapshot, quota requests) are proposed with exact parameters, cost and rollback, and run only through operator-approved directed actions (Agent Actions in the Operator Web App). There is no fixed waiting period between modifications; the next one is allowed once the previous one completes.\\\\n- **No interpretation without data:** report what couldn\\'t be checked and use fallbacks. AWS CloudTrail is optional; `DescribeVolumesModifications` is the change record.\\\\n- **Units:** MiB/s for throughput, stated every time.\\\\n- **Escalate** on scope signals or when the investigation can\\'t explain the symptom.\\\\n\\\\n## Error Handling\\\\n\\\\nErrors, gated reads and missing metrics are handled with the fallback table in [references/data-collection.md](references/data-collection.md). {"id": "b09eb10d-e3d9-4cbe-964c-4388d9eb9014", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_MjGXLdfMJ204ywcwBAwfDc", "content": "[{'text': '# Troubleshoot: encryption and AWS KMS\\n\\nBuilt from public documentation; not yet live-tested. Validate this path in a non-production account before relying on it.\\n\\n## When this path applies\\n\\n- An encrypted volume will not attach, or an instance with encrypted volumes will not start.\\n- Sharing an encrypted snapshot or AMI with another account fails, or the other account cannot use it.\\n- Questions about encryption by default.\\n- Encrypting an existing unencrypted volume, or changing the key of an encrypted one.\\n\\n## Procedure\\n\\n1. **Read the volume or snapshot.** `DescribeVolumes` or `DescribeSnapshots`: `Encrypted`, `KmsKeyId`.\\n2. **Read the key.** AWS KMS `DescribeKey` on `KmsKeyId`: `KeyState` (Enabled, Disabled, PendingDeletion), `KeyManager` (AWS or CUSTOMER), Region.\\n   - Disabled or pending deletion: the key cannot be used, so the volume cannot be attached or used. Recommend re-enabling the key or cancelling the deletion, as a proposal (see Safety rules).\\n3. **Read who may use the key.** `GetKeyPolicy` and `ListGrants`. The principal attaching or starting (the user or role, and the instance\\'s service path through Amazon EBS) must be allowed to use the key. Report the missing permission by name, as found in the policy.\\n4. **Sharing across accounts.**\\n   - A snapshot encrypted with the default AWS managed key cannot be shared. Copy it with a customer managed key first.\\n   - With a customer managed key, share the snapshot (`createVolumePermission`) and also allow the destination account in the key policy.\\n   - For cross-Region copies, the destination needs a key in the destination Region.\\n5. **Encryption by default.** `GetEbsEncryptionByDefault` and `GetEbsDefaultKmsKeyId` per Region. The setting is per Region and applies to new volumes and snapshot copies.\\n6. **Re-encrypting an existing volume.** There is no in-place change. Proposed steps: create a snapshot, copy it with encryption and the chosen key (or create a volume from the snapshot with encryption on), create the new volume, stop the application, swap the volumes, verify, then retire the old volume. The agent proposes these steps; it does not run them.\\n\\n## Decision rules\\n\\n- Key state first, then key policy and grants, then sharing.\\n- If the key is usable and permissions look correct, check whether the error mentions a different key ID than the one on the volume.\\n- Never suggest disabling encryption as a fix.\\n\\n## What to report\\n\\nThe verdict template in [finding-logic.md](finding-logic.md). Binding layer is \"Not applicable\" unless a performance question is also asked. Evidence includes the key ID as returned by the API, its state, its manager, and the policy statement or grant that is missing.\\n\\n## Safety rules\\n\\n- This path is read-only.\\n- No key policy change, grant change, key enable, deletion cancel, or encryption-by-default change runs without a directed action approved on the approval card.\\n- Never suggest disabling encryption or removing a key policy statement that other resources depend on.\\n\\n## Sources\\n\\n- Amazon EBS encryption: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-encryption.html\\n- How Amazon EBS encryption works: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/how-ebs-encryption-works.html\\n- Encryption by default: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/encryption-by-default.html\\n- Share the KMS key for an encrypted snapshot: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/share-kms-key.html\\n- Share a snapshot: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-modifying-snapshot-permissions.html\\n- Copy a snapshot: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-copy-snapshot.html\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_uHnBn2GVnQjyOx9p4F79nc", "content": "[{'text': '# Data collection: read-only APIs, metric math, errors and fallbacks\\n\\nLoad this file on every request. Every value in a verdict or a review comes from one of these calls. Tags are used for naming only, never as the source of a configuration value.\\n\\n## Read-only API allowlist\\n\\n| Service | APIs |\\n|---|---|\\n| Amazon EC2 | `DescribeVolumes`, `DescribeVolumeStatus`, `DescribeVolumesModifications`, `DescribeVolumeAttribute`, `DescribeInstances`, `DescribeInstanceTypes`, `DescribeInstanceAttribute`, `DescribeSnapshots`, `DescribeSnapshotAttribute`, `DescribeImages`, `DescribeFastSnapshotRestores`, `GetEbsEncryptionByDefault`, `GetEbsDefaultKmsKeyId`, `GetSnapshotBlockPublicAccessState`, `DescribeLockedSnapshots` |\\n| Amazon CloudWatch | `DescribeAlarms`, `DescribeAlarmHistory`, `GetMetricData`, `ListMetrics` |\\n| Service Quotas | `ListServiceQuotas`, `GetServiceQuota`, `GetAWSDefaultServiceQuota`, `ListRequestedServiceQuotaChangeHistoryByQuota` |\\n| Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager | `GetLifecyclePolicies`, `GetLifecyclePolicy` |\\n| Recycle Bin | `ListRules`, `GetRule` |\\n| AWS Backup | `ListBackupPlans`, `ListBackupSelections`, `GetBackupSelection`, `ListRecoveryPointsByResource` (always with `ManagedByAWSBackupOnly` set to true; without it the call also returns snapshots AWS Backup did not create), `ListProtectedResources` |\\n| AWS KMS | `DescribeKey`, `GetKeyPolicy`, `ListGrants` |\\n| AWS Cost Explorer | `GetCostAndUsage`, `GetDimensionValues` |\\n| AWS FIS | `ListExperiments`, `GetExperiment` |\\n| AWS Health | `DescribeEvents` |\\n| AWS Compute Optimizer (optional) | `GetEBSVolumeRecommendations` |\\n| AWS CloudTrail (optional) | `LookupEvents`. This call is optional. If it is denied or returns nothing, record a Gap and continue. Never make it a required step |\\n\\nNothing outside this list is called by the skill on its own. Mutating calls are proposals (see SKILL.md Critical rules).\\n\\n## Metric rules\\n\\nAWS/EBS publishes 1-minute data.\\n\\n| Namespace | Metrics | Dimensions |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| AWS/EBS | `VolumeAvgIOPS` (Ops/s), `VolumeAvgThroughput` (KiB/s), `VolumeAvgReadLatency`, `VolumeAvgWriteLatency` | `VolumeId` AND `InstanceId`. Nitro instances only |\\n| AWS/EBS | `VolumeReadOps`, `VolumeWriteOps`, `VolumeReadBytes`, `VolumeWriteBytes`, `VolumeTotalReadTime`, `VolumeTotalWriteTime`, `VolumeQueueLength`, `VolumeIdleTime`, `BurstBalance`, `VolumeThroughputPercentage` (Provisioned IOPS SSD only) | `VolumeId` |\\n| AWS/EC2 | `EBSIOBalance%`, `EBSByteBalance%`, `EBSReadOps`, `EBSWriteOps`, `EBSReadBytes`, `EBSWriteBytes` | `InstanceId` |\\n\\nMetric math from the Amazon CloudWatch metrics page for Amazon EBS. Use `Sum` statistics for ops, bytes and time.\\n\\n- IOPS = Sum(`VolumeReadOps` + `VolumeWriteOps`) / period in seconds\\n- MiB/s = Sum(`VolumeReadBytes` + `VolumeWriteBytes`) / period in seconds / 1,048,576\\n- Average latency per operation = `VolumeTotalReadTime` / `VolumeReadOps` (and the write equivalent)\\n- Idle percentage = Sum(`VolumeIdleTime`) / period in seconds x 100\\n- MiB/s from `VolumeAvgThroughput` = value in KiB/s / 1,024\\n\\nWhat a 1-minute average hides: sub-minute peaks can reach a limit while the minute average looks below it (micro-bursting). When latency or queue length rises while the average sits below the limit, say that headroom is not proven instead of claiming it.\\n\\n`EBSIOBalance%` and `EBSByteBalance%` are published only for some instance sizes (generally 4xlarge and smaller) that can burst. If they are absent, the instance does not publish them. That is not a fault.\\n\\n## Errors and fallbacks\\n\\n| What happens | What it means | What to do |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| `AccessDenied` on any call | The role cannot read that data | Name the exact API in Gaps. Continue with the rest |\\n| A read call is held behind an operator-approval gate (for example `dlm:GetLifecyclePolicies` or `rbin:ListRules`) | The Agent Space treats it as an action | Report it as a Gap and say which conclusion stays unconfirmed. Never ask the operator to bypass the gate |\\n| No `VolumeAvg*` data | The instance is not Nitro, or the `InstanceId` dimension is missing | Add `InstanceId`. If still empty, use the Sum-based math above |\\n| `EBSIOBalance%` absent | The instance size does not publish it | Compare the summed IOPS and MiB/s of all attached volumes to the `DescribeInstanceTypes` baseline |\\n| `DescribeInstanceTypes` values in MB/s | The API reports instance throughput in MB/s (bandwidth in Mbps) | Convert to MiB/s before comparing (1 MB/s = 1,000,000 bytes/s; 1 MiB/s = 1,048,576 bytes/s) |\\n| AWS CloudTrail optional lookup denied or empty | No access, or the event is outside retention | Use `DescribeVolumesModifications` for the change record. It is not bound by AWS CloudTrail retention |\\n| No metric data for a volume | The volume is new, detached, or the window is wrong | Check `DescribeVolumes` state and attachment times, widen the window, report the Gap |\\n\\n## Sources\\n\\n- Amazon CloudWatch metrics for Amazon EBS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/using_cloudwatch_ebs.html\\n- Instance metrics, including `EBSIOBalance%` and `EBSByteBalance%`: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/viewing_metrics_with_cloudwatch.html\\n- Amazon EBS-optimized instances (baseline and maximum, MB/s): https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-optimized.html\\n- Monitoring volume modifications: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/monitoring-volume-modifications.html\\n- AWS FIS actions: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fis/latest/userguide/fis-actions-reference.html\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}
